tasks.short: Inspect passenger tickets for destination information.

steps.what: Read the passenger ticket to obtain the destination.
Match ticket information to the booked destination on departure control.
Inspect passenger tickets in person to verify the traveller.

tasks.design: The gate agent already stores name, seat, and destination on the departure control record in {OTHER}. The flight attendant still reads the passenger ticket and still inspects the traveller at the door. The screen lookup is shorter because those three fields are already stored.
tasks.previous_blocker: The destination sat on the ticket and on a printed list, and the cabin screen did not show the record the gate had stored.
tasks.enabler_now: Check-in already writes name, seat, and destination before boarding. The cabin only needs that same record on a screen.
tasks.still_hard: A phone ticket can fail to open, and a name that does not match still needs the person at the door.
tasks.human_edge: The attendant sees whether the person in the doorway matches the ticket.

ambition.what: When the destination is already stored, tell a connecting passenger the onward airport in the same minute the ticket matches, including a phone ticket.

tasks.altitude: The door check stays. The attendant spends less of the lookup searching for a destination that check-in already stored.

reach.task: Check a traveller's ticket for destination
reach.learn: The ticket in the traveller's hand still has to be read. The screen only shortens the lookup.

evidence.claim: A departure control record can show the destination stored at check-in next to the name on the ticket. The attendant still compares that destination with the ticket. Model knowledge.

The ticket names a person. Using the record the gate already stored for this flight is the existing check. Copying those names into a new list to score the attendant would be a different purpose, and this design does not do that. Model knowledge.

assumptions: Means sum to 100. Largest remainder gives screens 5, documents 14, and in-person 81. Spreadsheet 0.1 and mail 0.1 are omitted; this check has no workbook and no e-mail.
The gate agent stores name, seat, and destination on the departure control record before boarding. That upkeep is other-role time, not a slice of the attendant's 100.
Only the screen lookup is shorter, and 40 percent of it remains because the attendant still opens the record and compares it with the ticket. Reading the ticket and the door check stay at full time.
No focal upkeep. The design adds no second list of passenger names and does not score the attendant.
unknowns: Whether this carrier shows the departure control record in the cabin, or only at the gate.
research_questions: Where is the departure control record visible to the cabin crew on this carrier?

already_counted.description: Comparing the ticket destination with the destination already stored on departure control.

incremental.description: The gate agent keeps name, seat, and destination on the departure control record for each flight.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low when departure control has no destination stored for that name, so the attendant still reads the ticket, still searches, and still checks the traveller at the door. High when the destination is already stored, the screen lookup is shorter, and the ticket reading and the door check stay at full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Count headsets, beverages, and money collected.

steps.what: Read opening headsets and beverages on the catering screen.
Count headsets, alcoholic beverages, and money in the galley.
File the inventory of headsets, beverages, and money collected.
Stop the workbook once the catering record holds those totals.

tasks.design: The aircraft service attendant posts the headset and beverage uplift on the catering record in {OTHER}. The flight attendant still counts the galley and still files the inventory of headsets, beverages, and money on {DOCS}, and confirms that file before it is kept. The workbook copy stops once that file holds the totals.
tasks.previous_blocker: Opening stock was counted again because the uplift was not on a screen the attendant could read, and the totals were then copied into a workbook.
tasks.enabler_now: Catering already counts the uplift when it loads the galley. The cabin count can start from those figures.
tasks.still_hard: Bottles, headsets, and cash still have to be counted by hand in the galley. A short count is a real variance the attendant must see.
tasks.human_edge: The attendant sees a broken headset, an open bottle, or cash that does not match the sales.

ambition.what: File a short headset or bottle count on the day the uplift is short, not only after the last sector.

tasks.altitude: The galley count stays. The filing stays, and the attendant still confirms it. The second copy into the workbook stops.

reach.task: Post the galley uplift before departure
reach.learn: Which headset and beverage figures the cabin count is compared with.

evidence.claim: A catering stock record can hold the headset and beverage uplift loaded before departure, so the cabin count compares with that uplift. Model knowledge.
Cash and alcohol totals are an internal stock record. National rules on keeping that record vary. This design does not score the attendant on the count. Model knowledge.

assumptions: Means sum to 100.1, so shares are scaled by 100/100.1 before largest remainder: screens 8, spreadsheets 5, documents 15, in-person 72. Mail 0.2 is omitted; the count is not e-mailed.
The aircraft service attendant posts the headset and beverage uplift before departure. That upkeep is other-role time, not a slice of the attendant's 100.

Only the opening-stock lookup is shorter, at 40 percent remaining. The galley count and the filing stay at full time. The workbook stops because the filed inventory already holds the totals, and that stop writes no new record.
No focal upkeep. The filing is the attendant's own confirmation of the final count. The design does not score the attendant on speed or shortage.
unknowns: Whether national rules require the bar inventory to stay on paper as well as in the document store.
research_questions: Which headset, beverage, and cash fields does the catering uplift already store before departure?

already_counted.description: Reading the posted uplift and comparing it with what the galley count will check.
Confirming the filed totals for headsets, beverages, and money before the file is kept.

incremental.description: The aircraft service attendant posts the headset and beverage uplift on the catering record before each departure.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low when the catering screen has no opening uplift, so the attendant still builds the opening list and still copies totals into the workbook. High when the uplift is posted, the workbook stops, and the galley count and the filing stay at full time.

approvals.approved_version: filed inventory of headsets, beverages, and money

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Sell alcoholic beverages to passengers and judge each request.
Charge the beverage on the cabin point-of-sale screen.
Stop the separate price list once the screen shows the tariff.

tasks.design: The cabin service supervisor loads the drink tariff on the point-of-sale screen in {OTHER}. The flight attendant still sells alcoholic beverages to passengers and still judges each sale in the cabin. The separate price list on {DOCS} stops. The charge is its own step, confirmed by the attendant before it is taken.
tasks.previous_blocker: The price sat on a separate list, so the attendant looked it up apart from the charge.
tasks.enabler_now: The bar tariff is a fixed list for the flight. The point-of-sale screen can show it without a new way of selling.
tasks.still_hard: Age and intoxication are judged at the seat. A price on a screen does not make that decision.
tasks.human_edge: The attendant refuses a sale when the passenger should not be served.
tasks.altitude: The sale stays. The charge stays, and the attendant still confirms the amount. The separate price list stops.

reach.task: Set the drink tariff for the flight
reach.learn: Which drinks the tariff lists before the attendant judges the passenger.

evidence.claim: A cabin point-of-sale screen can show a drink price loaded before the flight. The attendant still decides whether to sell. Model knowledge.
Serving alcohol stays a judgement by the attendant. A price on a screen does not make that decision. National rules on age and intoxication vary. Model knowledge.

assumptions: Means sum to 100. Largest remainder gives screens 2, documents 2, and in-person 96. Spreadsheet 0.1 and mail 0.1 are omitted; the sale is not e-mailed and has no workbook.
The cabin service supervisor loads the drink tariff on the point-of-sale screen before boarding. That upkeep is other-role time, not a slice of the attendant's 100.
The sale and the charge stay at full time. The price list stops because the tariff is already on the charge screen, and that stop writes no new record.
No focal upkeep. The charge confirmation is the attendant's own check of the amount. The design does not record which attendant sold which drink in order to score them.
unknowns: Whether the point-of-sale device stores the passenger name with the drink, and whether national rules require a paper price list to be kept.
research_questions: Does the point-of-sale tariff include every alcoholic drink the attendant may sell on this flight?

already_counted.description: Confirming the drink and the amount on the point-of-sale charge before it is taken.

incremental.description: The cabin service supervisor loads the drink tariff on the point-of-sale screen before each flight.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low when the point-of-sale screen has no drink tariff, so the attendant still reads the price list while the sale and the charge stay at full time. High when the tariff is on the screen, the price list stops, and the sale and the charge stay at full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The flight attendant still reads each ticket at the door, still counts the galley, and still judges each drink sale. Departure control only shortens the destination lookup. The catering record only shortens the opening-stock lookup. The point-of-sale screen only retires the separate price list.
reach: Passenger Attendants: a ticket destination still has to be read from the pass the traveller holds.
Aircraft Service Attendants: the galley uplift is the list the cabin count is compared with.
First-Line Supervisors of Passenger Attendants: the drink tariff is loaded before the attendant judges a sale.
skills_to_grow: Match a ticket destination to the stored destination, not only the printed name.
Count cash and bottles against the posted uplift before filing the inventory.
Judge the passenger before confirming the charge.
role.ambitious_version: On a flight where destinations are already stored, the attendant tells connecting passengers the onward airport before they ask at the door.
